Posterior draws from a Bayesian calibration

Source: R/cal.draws.R
cal.draws.Rd

Returns the posterior draws of a Bayesian calibration as a data.frame, in the same shape as the results of the bootstrap calibrations (cal.ols() and others). The result can be passed to rec.bayesian(), rec.clumped(), or cal.ci().

Usage

cal.draws(fit, model = NULL, newMaterial = FALSE)

Arguments

fit

A result from cal.bayesian() or cal.ion.bayesian(), or a single stanfit from it.

model

The model to use when fit holds more than one. Use "errors", "noerrors", "mixed_errors", or "mixed_noerrors", or the name of the element (such as "BLM1_fit").

newMaterial

For mixed models, whether to return draws for a material that is not in the calibration. These draws combine the uncertainty in the shared means with the spread among materials.

Value

A data.frame with one row per draw and the columns alpha, beta, and sigma. Models with a second predictor also have gamma. Mixed models have one set of draws per material, stacked, with a Material column. With newMaterial = TRUE, there is a single set of draws and no Material column.

Examples

# \donttest{
ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S1", nobs = 50, seed = 1)
fit <- cal.bayesian(ds, models = "errors", numSavedSteps = 1000)
#> Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)): error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'sampling': Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')
head(cal.draws(fit))
#> Error: object 'fit' not found
# }
